rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadiyya is a gift offered as a gesture of courtesy and affection.
rows.anchor: والهدية هي: العطية على طريق الملاطفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghawī portrays Bilqīs as intelligent and politically experienced.
rows.anchor: بلقيس كانت امرأة لبيبة قد سيست وساست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bilqīs meant to conciliate Sulaymān away from her kingdom and test whether he was a king or prophet: a king would accept and depart, while a prophet would refuse and require them to follow his religion.
rows.anchor: أي: إلى سليمان وقومه، بهدية أصانعه بها عن ملكي وأختبره بها أملك هو أم نبي؟

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the attendants wore identical clothes so no one could tell male from female.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس (2) ألبستهم لباسا واحدا كي لا يعرف ذكر من أنثى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the boys wore girls’ clothes and the girls wore boys’ clothes.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: ألبس الغلمان لباس الجواري وألبس الجواري لباس الغلمان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās gives the retinue as one hundred male attendants and one hundred female attendants.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: مائة وصيف ومائة وصيفة

rows.speaker: مجاهد ومقاتل
rows.claim: Mujāhid and Muqātil give the retinue as two hundred boys and two hundred girls.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: [ومقاتل]

rows.speaker: قتادة وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Qatāda and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr say she sent a gold ingot wrapped in silk and brocade.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة، وسعيد بن جبير: أرسلت إليه بلبنة من ذهب في حرير وديباج

rows.speaker: ثابت البناني
rows.claim: Thābit al-Bunānī says the gift was gold plates in brocade containers.
rows.anchor: وقال ثابت البناني: أهدت إليه صفائح من الذهب في أوعية الديباج

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says the gift consisted of four gold ingots.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كانت أربع لبنات من ذهب

rows.speaker: وهب وغيره
rows.claim: Wahb and others describe five hundred cross-dressed boys and girls, adorned with gold and gems and mounted on five hundred mares and five hundred barādhīn; the gifts also included gold and silver ingots, a jeweled crown, perfumes, a pearl, and an agate bead.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب وغيره: عمدت بلقيس إلى خمسمائة غلام وخمسمائة جارية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bilqīs sent the gifts with the noble al-Mundhir ibn ʿAmr and advisers, and wrote prophetic tests: identify the attendants, disclose the box’s contents, drill a straight hole in the pearl, and thread the crooked bead unaided.
rows.anchor: ودعت رجلا من أشراف قومها يقال له المنذر بن عمرو، وضمت إليه، رجالا من قومها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She instructed the boys to speak effeminately like women and the girls to speak roughly like men when Sulaymān addressed them.
rows.anchor: وأمرت بلقيس الغلمان، فقالت: إذا كلمكم سليمان فكلموه بكلام تأنيث وتخنيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza and Yaʿqūb read with one doubled nūn and retain the yāʾ; the others read two light nūns, with Ḥijāzī and Baṣran readers retaining the yāʾ and the rest dropping it.
rows.anchor: بنون واحدة مشددة وإثبات الياء، وقرأ الآخرون: بنونين خفيفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God gave Sulaymān means prophethood, religion, wisdom, and kingship, all superior to what they brought.
rows.anchor: أعطاني الله من النبوة والدين والحكمة والملك، {خير} أفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people rejoice in gifts as worldly boasting and rivalry; Sulaymān does not need or delight in worldly wealth, since God gave him abundant dominion and honored him with religion and prophethood.
rows.anchor: لأنكم أهل مفاخرة في الدنيا ومكاثرة بها، تفرحون بإهداء بعضكم لبعض، فأما أنا فلا أفرح بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sulaymān tells al-Mundhir, the delegation’s leader, to return to Bilqīs and her people.
rows.anchor: ثم قال للمنذر بن عمرو وأمير الوفد: {ارجع إليهم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites would become leaders in goodness whom others follow.
rows.anchor: قادة في الخير يقتدى بهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda interprets the leaders as rulers and kings, citing God’s statement that He made them kings.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: ولاة وملوكا، دليله: قوله عز وجل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid interprets them as callers to goodness.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: دعاة إلى الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They would inherit Pharaoh and his people’s property and dwellings.
rows.anchor: يعني: أملاك فرعون وقومه يخلفونهم في مساكنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God would settle the Israelites in Egypt and Syria as places where they could reside.
rows.anchor: نوطن لهم في أرض مصر والشام، ونجعلها لهم مكانا يستقرون فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read the verb in the third person with Pharaoh, Hāmān, and their troops as subjects; the others read first-person plural with those names as objects.
rows.anchor: بالنون وضمها، وكسر الراء، ونصب الياء ونصب ما بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥadhar means guarding oneself against harm; Pharaoh’s people had been warned their destruction would come by an Israelite man and feared him, so God showed them what they dreaded.
rows.anchor: والحذر هو التوقي من الضرر، وذلك أنهم أخبروا أن هلاكهم على يد رجل من بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: آسية
rows.claim: The account says Āsiya named the child Mūsā because they found him among water and trees, glossing the name’s parts as water and tree.
rows.anchor: فقيل لآسية سميه فقالت: سميته موسى لأنا وجدناه في الماء والشجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city is the place where Moses had killed the Copt.
rows.anchor: أي: في المدينة التي قتل فيها القبطي،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses feared being killed because he had killed the Copt; tarraqub means awaiting something bad.
rows.anchor: من قتله القبطي، {يترقب} ينتظر سوءا، والترقب: انتظار المكروه

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says Moses was waiting to see when he would be seized for the killing.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: ينتظر متى يؤخذ به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelite was calling for Moses’ help and crying out to him from a distance.
rows.anchor: يستغيثه ويصيح به من بعد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Pharaoh demanded a killer and witnesses for the slain Egyptian, refusing to judge without proof; Moses then met the same Israelite fighting another Egyptian and regretted the previous day’s killing.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أتي فرعون فقيل له: إن بني إسرائيل قتلوا منا رجلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghawī prefers that Moses addressed the Israelite: he was plainly at fault for involving Moses in yesterday’s killing and now seeking help in another fight; most exegetes agree.
rows.anchor: والأول أصوب، وعليه الأكثرون أنه قال ذلك للإسرائيلي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says Moses called the Egyptian plainly misguided because of his oppression.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنما قال موسى للفرعوني: إنك لغوي مبين بظلمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses felt compassion for the Israelite and reached to strike the Egyptian.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن موسى أدركته الرقة (1) بالإسرائيلي فمد يده ليبطش بالفرعوني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelite thought Moses was about to strike him because Moses was angry and had called him plainly misguided.
rows.anchor: فظن الإسرائيلي أنه يريد أن يبطش به لما رأى من غضبه وسمع قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here being a tyrant on earth means killing unjustly.
rows.anchor: {إلا أن تكون جبارا في الأرض} بالقتل ظلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Egyptian heard the Israelite’s words, realized Moses had killed the Egyptian the previous day, informed Pharaoh, and Pharaoh ordered Moses killed.
rows.anchor: فلما سمع القبطي ما قال الإسرائيلي علم أن موسى هوالذي قتل ذلك الفرعوني

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Pharaoh sent executioners after Moses, who took the main road.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فلما أرسل فرعون الذباحين لقتل موسى أخذوا الطريق الأعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man who came was one of Moses’ adherents and came from the far end of the city.
rows.anchor: من شيعة موسى، {من أقصى المدينة} أي: من آخرها

rows.speaker: أكثر أهل التأويل
rows.claim: Most exegetes identify him as Ḥizbīl, a believer from Pharaoh’s household.
rows.anchor: قال أكثر أهل التأويل: اسمه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other accounts name the man Shimʿūn or Shimʿān.
rows.anchor: وقيل: اسمه "شمعون"، وقيل: "شمعان"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He was hurrying on foot, took a nearby route, reached Moses first, and warned him to use another route.
rows.anchor: أي: يسرع في مشيه، فأخذ طريقا قريبا حتى سبق إلى موسى فأخبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The notables were consulting about Moses and planning his death.
rows.anchor: يعني: أشراف قوم فرعون يتشاورون فيك، {ليقتلوك}

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the expression as people ordering one another to kill Moses.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: يأمر بعضهم بعضا بقتلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man’s counsel was that Moses leave the city.
rows.anchor: {فاخرج} من المدينة، {إني لك من الناصحين} في الأمر لك بالخروج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses left the city fearing and expecting pursuit; the oppressive people he asks God to save him from are the unbelievers.
rows.anchor: خائفا يترقب} أي: ينتظر الطلب، {قال رب نجني من القوم الظالمين} الكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the story, Pharaoh sent people after Moses and told them to ride the mountain passes, since Moses did not know the route.
rows.anchor: وفي القصة: أن فرعون بعث في طلبه حين أخبر بهربه فقال اركبوا ثنيات الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tijāha Midian means heading toward it; a house is said to be tilqāʾ another when it faces it, from the root of meeting.
rows.anchor: أي: قصد نحوها ماضيا إليها، يقال: داره تلقاء دار فلان، إذا كانت محاذيتها

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says Moses took the road that faces Midian.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: يعني سلك الطريق الذي تلقاء مدين فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Midian was a son of Abraham, and the town was named after him.
rows.anchor: ومدين هو مدين بن إبراهيم، سميت البلدة باسمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses fled without a mount, shoes, or provisions; Midian was eight days’ journey from Egypt.
rows.anchor: وكان موسى قد خرج خائفا بلا ظهر ولا حذاء ولا زاد، وكانت مدين على مسيرة ثمانية أيام من مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asked for guidance to the route to Midian because he had not known the way there; an angel carrying a staff then led him to it.
rows.anchor: أي: قصد الطريق إلى مدين، قال ذلك لأنه لم يكن يعرف الطريق إليها قبل

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The exegetes say Moses had only leaves and greens to eat, saw their greenness in his belly, and wore through his soles before reaching Midian.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: خرج موسى من مصر ولم يكن له طعام إلا ورق الشجر والبقل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says this journey was Moses’ first trial from God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: وهو أول ابتلاء من الله عز وجل لموسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God would strengthen Moses through his brother Aaron, who was then in Egypt.
rows.anchor: أي: نقويك بأخيك، وكان هارون يومئذ بمصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sultan here means an argument and proof.
rows.anchor: حجة وبرهانا، {فلا يصلون إليكما بآياتنا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because of God’s signs, Pharaoh’s people could not reach Moses and Aaron with killing or harm.
rows.anchor: أي: لا يصلون إليكما بقتل ولا سوء لمكان آياتنا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another syntactic analysis places the phrase out of its apparent order: authority is granted through the miracles, so they cannot reach the two.
rows.anchor: وقيل: فيه تقديم وتأخير، تقديره: ونجعل لكما سلطانا بآياتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses, Aaron, and their followers would prevail over Pharaoh and his people.
rows.anchor: أنتما ومن اتبعكما الغالبون} أي: لكما ولأتباعكما الغلبة على فرعون وقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s people called the signs fabricated magic, meaning invented; their claim that they had never heard this concerned Moses’ call.
rows.anchor: واضحات، {قالوا ما هذا إلا سحر مفترى} مختلق، {وما سمعنا بهذا} بالذي تدعونا إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meccan readers omit the conjunction wāw before Moses’ reply, as do their codices.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل مكة بغير واو، وكذلك هو في مصاحفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says God knows who is right and who is wrong, and who will have the praiseworthy final outcome in the afterlife; oppressors means unbelievers.
rows.anchor: بالمحق من المبطل، {ومن تكون له عاقبة الدار} العقبى المحمودة في الدار الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to fire bricks; one account says Pharaoh was the first to make and build with bricks.
rows.anchor: فاطبخ لي الآجر، وقيل: إنه أول من اتخذ من الآجر وبنى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ṣarḥ is a high palace; another explanation is a tower or lighthouse.
rows.anchor: قصرا عاليا، وقيل: منارة

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Exegetes recount that Hāmān gathered fifty thousand builders plus crews, raised an unprecedented tower, and Pharaoh shot an arrow skyward that returned bloodied; he claimed to have killed Moses’ God, then Gabriel struck the tower apart, killing its workers and a million soldiers.
rows.anchor: قال أهل التفسير (1) لما أمر فرعون وزيره هامان ببناء الصرح، جمع هامان العمال والفعلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh meant that he would look at Moses’ God and determine His condition.
rows.anchor: أنظر إليه وأقف على حاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one Pharaoh calls a liar is Moses, for claiming that the earth and creation have a god other than Pharaoh and that he is God’s messenger.
rows.anchor: يعني موسى، {من الكاذبين} في زعمه أن للأرض والخلق إلها غيري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God asks where the partners the people had claimed in worldly life are.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا أنهم شركائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those upon whom punishment has become due are the leaders of misguidance; the people they misled are their followers, whom they called to error.
rows.anchor: وجب عليهم العذاب وهم رءوس الضلالة، {ربنا هؤلاء الذين أغوينا} أي: دعوناهم إلى الغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leaders say they misled their followers just as they themselves were misguided, then disown them; the groups become enemies of one another.
rows.anchor: أضللناهم كما ضللنا، {تبرأنا إليك} منهم {ما كانوا إيانا يعبدون} برئ بعضهم من بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers are told to call their idols to save them from punishment, but the idols do not answer.
rows.anchor: {وقيل} للكفار: {ادعوا شركاءكم} أي: الأصنام لتخلصكم من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apodosis of law is omitted: had they been guided in worldly life, they would not have seen the punishment.
rows.anchor: على تقدير: لو أنهم كانوا يهتدون في الدنيا ما رأوا العذاب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God asks the disbelievers what response they gave the messengers.
rows.anchor: أي: يسأل الله الكفار، {فيقول ماذا أجبتم المرسلين}

words: إِنَّ قَٰرُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوْمِ مُوسَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghawī says Qarūn was Moses’ cousin and gives their shared lineage through Qāhith and Yaṣhar.
rows.anchor: كان ابن عمه؛ لأنه قارون بن يصهر

words: إِنَّ قَٰرُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوْمِ مُوسَىٰ
rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq instead says Qarūn was Moses’ paternal uncle, Amram’s brother, and both were sons of Yaṣhar.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: كان قارون عم موسى، كان أخا عمران، وهما ابنا يصهر

words: إِنَّ قَٰرُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوْمِ مُوسَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarūn was the most learned Israelite in Torah, but became a hypocrite like al-Sāmirī.
rows.anchor: ولم يكن في بني إسرائيل أقرأ للتوراة من قارون، ولكنه نافق كما نافق السامري

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account says Qarūn was Pharaoh’s agent over the Israelites and oppressed them.
rows.anchor: قيل: كان عاملا لفرعون على بني إسرائيل، فكان يبغي عليهم ويظلمهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says Qarūn transgressed against them through his wealth.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: بغى عليهم بكثرة المال

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says Qarūn transgressed through associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: بغى عليهم بالشرك

rows.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
rows.claim: Shahr ibn Ḥawshab says Qarūn transgressed by lengthening his garment by a handspan.
rows.anchor: وقال شهر بن حوشب: زاد في طول ثيابه شبرا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿUmar quotes the Prophet saying that God will not look on Resurrection Day at one who drags his garment out of pride.
rows.anchor: وروينا عن ابن عمر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says Qarūn transgressed through pride and arrogance.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بغى عليهم بالكبر والعلو

rows.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد وجماعة
rows.claim: Qatāda, Mujāhid, and others take mafātiḥ as the keys used to open doors.
rows.anchor: هذا قول قتادة ومجاهد وجماعة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes mafātiḥ as the treasuries, as in 6:59.
rows.anchor: وقيل: مفاتحه: خزائنه، كما قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keys were so heavy they burdened and tilted the strong group carrying them.
rows.anchor: أي: لتثقلهم، وتميل بهم إذا حملوها لثقلها

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda calls the wording inverted: the group is weighed down by the keys; nāʾa means to rise under a heavy burden.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: هذا من المقلوب، تقديره: ما إن العصبة لتنوء بها

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid defines the group as ten to fifteen people.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: ما بين العشرة إلى خمسة عشر

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, transmitting from Ibn ʿAbbās, gives the range as three to ten.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: ما بين الثلاثة إلى العشرة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda defines the group as ten to forty people.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: ما بين العشرة إلى الأربعين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says the group consisted of forty men; another says seventy.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أربعون رجلا. وقيل: سبعون.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that forty of the strongest men carried Qarūn’s keys.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: كان يحمل مفاتحه أربعون رجلا أقوى ما يكون من الرجال

rows.speaker: خيثمة
rows.claim: Khaythama says he found in the Gospel that Qarūn’s treasury keys loaded sixty mules, each key no longer than a finger and each opening a treasure.
rows.anchor: وقال جرير عن منصور عن خيثمة، قال: وجدت في الإنجيل أن مفاتيح خزائن قارون

rows.speaker: ويقال
rows.claim: One account says Qarūn carried the keys everywhere; after iron became too heavy, he tried wood, then cowhide, and the keys went with him on forty mules.
rows.anchor: ويقال: كان قارون أينما ذهب يحمل معه مفاتيح كنوزه، وكانت من حديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command not to rejoice means not to become arrogant, insolent, or frolicsome.
rows.anchor: لا تبطر ولا تأشر ولا تمرح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disfavored rejoicers are arrogant people who do not thank God for what He has given them.
rows.anchor: الأشرين البطرين الذين لا يشكرون الله على ما أعطاهم

words: وَٱبْتَغِ فِيمَآ ءَاتَىٰكَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلدَّارَ ٱلْءَاخِرَةَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Use the wealth and blessings God gave to seek the afterlife by thanking Him and spending in what pleases Him.
rows.anchor: اطلب فيما أعطاك الله من الأموال والنعمة والجنة وهو أن تقوم بشكر الله

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
rows.claim: Mujāhid and Ibn Zayd say not to abandon worldly work for the afterlife, since a person’s true worldly share is working for the afterlife and escape from punishment.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد، وابن زيد: لا تترك أن تعمل في الدنيا للآخرة حتى تنجو من العذاب

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī interprets the worldly share as almsgiving and maintaining kinship.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: بالصدقة وصلة الرحم

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī says to use health, strength, youth, and wealth to seek the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقال علي: لا تنس صحتك وقوتك وشبابك وغناك أن تطلب بها الآخرة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Amr ibn Maymūn al-Awdī reports the Prophet advising a man to seize five before five: youth before old age, health before illness, wealth before poverty, free time before busyness, and life before death; Baghawī calls the report mursal.
rows.anchor: عن عمرو بن ميمون الأودي قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لرجل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says one should give the surplus while keeping what suffices.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: أمر أن يقدم الفضل ويمسك ما يغنيه

rows.speaker: منصور بن زاذان
rows.claim: Manṣūr ibn Zādhān says a person’s share of this world is provision for oneself and one’s family.
rows.anchor: قال منصور بن زاذان في قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The instruction means to do good through obedience to God, as God has done good through His blessings.
rows.anchor: [أي: أحسن بطاعة الله] (3) كما أحسن الله إليك بنعمته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported explanation says to do good to the Fire as God has done good to you.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أحسن إلى النار كما أحسن الله إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone who disobeys God has sought corruption in the earth.
rows.anchor: من عصى الله فقد طلب الفساد في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarūn claims his wealth came from merit and goodness God knew in him, deeming him worthy and favoring him with wealth as with other gifts.
rows.anchor: أي: على فضل وخير علمه الله عندي فرآني أهلا لذلك، ففضلني بهذا المال

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: One view takes the knowledge as alchemy: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab says Moses taught one third each to Joshua, Caleb, and Qarūn; Qarūn tricked the other two into combining their shares, producing his wealth.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن المسيب: كان موسى يعلم الكيمياء فعلم يوشع بن نون ثلث ذلك العلم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says Qarūn meant his knowledge of trade, farming, and other kinds of earning.
rows.anchor: وقيل: "على علم عندي" بالتصرف في التجارات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God had destroyed earlier unbelieving generations that were stronger and possessed greater wealth and numbers than Qarūn.
rows.anchor: الكافرة، {من هو أشد منه قوة وأكثر جمعا} للأموال

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says criminals enter the Fire without reckoning or questioning.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: يدخلون النار بغير حساب ولا سؤال

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the angels do not ask about them because they recognize the criminals by their marks.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: يعني لا يسأل الملائكة عنهم، لأنهم يعرفونهم بسيماهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says they are not asked to obtain information; the questioning is for rebuke and reproach.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: لا يسألون سؤال استعلام وإنما يسألون سؤال تقريع وتوبيخ

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies those endowed with knowledge as the Israelite scholars.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: يعني الأحبار من بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says they knew what God had promised in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: أوتوا العلم بما وعد الله في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They tell those who coveted Qarūn’s worldly wealth that God’s reward is better for whoever believes in His oneness and does righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: يعني ما عند الله من الثواب والجزاء خير {لمن آمن} وصدق بتوحيد الله

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil reads it as saying that only the patient receive righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: لا يؤتاها، يعني الأعمال الصالحة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says the patient are the ones granted this reward in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي لا يعطاها في الآخرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the referent as the statement that God’s reward is better; only those patient in obedience and resisting worldly adornment can say it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا يؤتى هذه الكلمة وهي قوله:

rows.speaker: أهل العلم بالأخبار
rows.claim: Traditionists portray Qarūn as Israel’s most learned man after Moses and Aaron, learned in Torah, handsome, wealthy, pleasant-voiced, and transgressive.
rows.anchor: قال أهل العلم بالأخبار: كان قارون أعلم بني إسرائيل بعد موسى وهارون

rows.speaker: أهل العلم بالأخبار
rows.claim: The account says God commanded blue threads at the four corners of Israelite garments to remind them of Him and revelation descending from heaven; Moses proposed green garments, but God warned that disobedience in a small command foretold disobedience in a great one.
rows.anchor: قال أهل العلم بالأخبار: كان قارون أعلم بني إسرائيل بعد موسى وهارون

rows.speaker: أهل العلم بالأخبار
rows.claim: Qarūn refused the garment command, saying only gods use such tokens to distinguish themselves; the account calls this the beginning of his rebellion.
rows.anchor: قال أهل العلم بالأخبار: كان قارون أعلم بني إسرائيل بعد موسى وهارون

rows.speaker: أهل العلم بالأخبار
rows.claim: After the sea crossing, Aaron received the high priesthood; Qarūn resented Moses’ message and Aaron’s priesthood and demanded proof that God had appointed Aaron.
rows.anchor: قال أهل العلم بالأخبار: كان قارون أعلم بني إسرائيل بعد موسى وهارون

rows.speaker: أهل العلم بالأخبار
rows.claim: Moses set the leaders’ staffs in his worship tent overnight; Aaron’s almond staff sprouted leaves, but Qarūn dismissed the sign as magic.
rows.anchor: قال أهل العلم بالأخبار: كان قارون أعلم بني إسرائيل بعد موسى وهارون

rows.speaker: أهل العلم بالأخبار
rows.claim: Qarūn separated from Moses with his followers and continually harassed him; Moses bore it because of kinship, while Qarūn grew more defiant and hostile.
rows.anchor: قال أهل العلم بالأخبار: كان قارون أعلم بني إسرائيل بعد موسى وهارون

rows.speaker: أهل العلم بالأخبار
rows.claim: Qarūn built a house with a gold door and gold-plated walls, where Israel’s leaders came morning and evening for food and conversation.
rows.anchor: قال أهل العلم بالأخبار: كان قارون أعلم بني إسرائيل بعد موسى وهارون

rows.speaker: وفي رواية
rows.claim: One version says the earth swallowed Qarūn’s bed first and then took him and his companions progressively to the knees, waist, and neck as they begged Moses; Qarūn appealed to God and kinship seventy times, but Moses ignored him in anger.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية: كان على سريره وفرشه فأخذته حتى غيبت سريره ثم قال: يا أرض خذيهم

rows.speaker: الله
rows.claim: God reproached Moses for his hard heart, saying Qarūn had appealed seventy times without relief, and that He would have answered if Qarūn had appealed to Him once.
rows.anchor: وأوحى الله إلى موسى ما أغلظ قلبك استغاث بك سبعين مرة فلم تغثه

rows.speaker: بعض الآثار
rows.claim: Some traditions add God’s declaration that He would not make the earth obedient to anyone after Moses.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الآثار: لا أجعل الأرض بعدك طوعا لأحد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says Qarūn sinks a man’s height into the earth each day and will not reach its bottom before the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: خسف به فهو يتجلجل في الأرض كل يوم قامة رجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Israelites whispered that Moses had invoked the sinking only to seize Qarūn’s estate, Moses prayed and God sank his house, treasures, and wealth as well.
rows.anchor: وأصبحت بنو إسرائيل يتناجون فيما بينهم أن موسى إنما دعا على قارون ليستبد بداره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fiʾa means a group, and those who could not help Qarūn could not protect him from God’s sinking.
rows.anchor: {فما كان له من فئة} جماعة، {ينصرونه من دون الله} يمنعونه من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muntaṣirīn means those able to defend themselves against the sinking that struck them.
rows.anchor: {وما كان من المنتصرين} الممتنعين مما نزل به من الخسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The misleaders carry the sins of their own deeds and the sins of those they led astray and turned from God’s path; this parallels 16:25, and the question about their inventions is rebuke.
rows.anchor: أوزار أعمالهم التي عملوها بأنفسهم، {وأثقالا مع أثقالهم} أي: أوزار من أضلوا وصدوا عن سبيل الله
